questions.question: Why did Aristotle leave Athens after Plato's death, according to the article?
options: He was disappointed with the Academy's direction and possibly influenced by anti-Macedonian sentiment.
He was expelled by the Athenian government for his impiety.
He wanted to travel to Persia to study eastern philosophy.
He was invited by Alexander the Great to tutor him in Pella.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that the traditional story records he was disappointed with the academy's direction after control passed to Speusippus, and it was possible that anti-Macedonian sentiments also influenced his decision.
Incorrect. The article mentions he was denounced for impiety later, after Alexander's death, but that was not the reason for his departure after Plato's death.
Incorrect. The article says he went to Assos in Asia Minor, not Persia, and there is no mention of a desire to study eastern philosophy.
Incorrect. He was invited to tutor Alexander later, in 343/42 BC, but that was not the reason for his departure from Athens after Plato's death.

questions.question: What does the nickname 'mind of the school' given to Aristotle by Plato imply about his role at the Academy?
options: He was recognized as a leading intellectual figure among researchers and lecturers.
He was the official head of the school after Plato's death.
He was the youngest student ever admitted to the Academy.
He was primarily focused on physical training in the gymnasium.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says he 'became distinguished as a researcher and lecturer, earning for himself the nickname "mind of the school"', indicating his intellectual prominence.
Incorrect. The article states that after Plato's death, control passed to Plato's nephew Speusippus, not Aristotle.
Incorrect. The article does not mention his age relative to other students, only that he joined at seventeen or eighteen.
Incorrect. The nickname refers to his intellectual contributions, not physical training.

questions.question: Why did Aristotle rent the Lyceum rather than buy property in Athens?
options: Because as a metic, he was not allowed to own property in Athens.
Because he wanted to save money for his library.
Because the Lyceum was the only building available for his school.
Because he planned to leave Athens soon and did not want a permanent residence.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article explicitly states: 'As a metic, Aristotle could not own property in Athens and thus rented a building known as the Lyceum'.
Incorrect. The article does not mention financial motives for renting.
Incorrect. The article does not say it was the only available building.
Incorrect. He stayed for twelve years, so he likely intended a long-term arrangement.

questions.question: What does the article imply about the relationship between Aristotle's family background and his early interest in biology?
options: His father's medical profession likely influenced his interest in biology and medicine.
His guardian Proxenus taught him biology as a child.
His mother's origins from Chalcis sparked his interest in marine biology.
His time at the Academy was the sole reason for his interest in biology.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says Nicomachus was 'likely responsible for Aristotle's early interest in biology and medicine' because he belonged to the medical guild of Asclepiadae.
Incorrect. The article does not mention Proxenus teaching him biology.
Incorrect. His mother's origins are mentioned but not linked to his interest in biology.
Incorrect. The article suggests his family background, not the Academy, was the likely influence.

questions.question: Why did Aristotle leave Athens at the end of his life, and what did he mean by his statement about not allowing the Athenians to sin twice against philosophy?
options: He fled to Chalcis after being denounced for impiety, and he was referring to the Athenians' execution of Socrates as the first sin.
He left because he was appointed as an ambassador to Macedon, and he meant he wanted to avoid political conflict.
He left to join Alexander's campaign in Persia, and he meant he wanted to protect his philosophical works from being destroyed.
He left because of a plague in Athens, and he meant he wanted to preserve his health for further philosophical work.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states he was denounced for impiety and fled to Chalcis, saying 'I will not allow the Athenians to sin twice against philosophy' â a reference to the trial and execution of Socrates.
Incorrect. There is no mention of an ambassadorship.
Incorrect. He did not join Alexander's campaign; he fled to Chalcis.
Incorrect. The article does not mention a plague.

questions.question: What does the article suggest about the survival and transmission of Aristotle's works?
options: His works were hidden for protection and later purchased by a collector, while copies of major works circulated.
All his works were published during his lifetime and widely distributed.
His works were destroyed by the Athenians after his death.
His works were preserved only by Alexander the Great's personal library.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says his papers were hidden for protection until purchased by Apellicon, and many copies of major works had already begun to circulate.
Incorrect. The article states that only a third of his original output survived, and none was intended for publication.
Incorrect. There is no mention of destruction by Athenians.
Incorrect. The article does not mention Alexander's library.

questions.question: Why is Aristotle considered the founder of the Peripatetic school, and what does the name 'Peripatetic' derive from?
options: He established his school in the Lyceum, and the name comes from the colonnade (peripatos) in the building.
He was a wandering teacher, and the name means 'traveler'.
He founded the school in Stagira, and the name comes from the Greek word for 'philosophy'.
He was the first to teach while walking, and the name means 'walking teacher'.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says the school acquired the name 'Peripatetic' from the colonnade (peripatos) in the Lyceum where he taught.
Incorrect. The name is not derived from traveling.
Incorrect. The school was in Athens, not Stagira.
Incorrect. The article specifically says the name comes from the colonnade, not from walking.

questions.question: What does the article imply about Aristotle's influence on medieval scholarship and theology?
options: His views shaped medieval scholarship, and he was revered by both Muslim and Christian scholars.
His works were largely ignored until the Renaissance.
His influence was limited to logic and did not extend to theology.
His physical science was replaced by classical mechanics during the Middle Ages.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states his views profoundly shaped medieval scholarship, and he was revered among medieval Muslim scholars as 'The First Teacher' and among Christians as 'The Philosopher'.
Incorrect. The article says his influence extended from late antiquity into the Renaissance.
Incorrect. The article mentions his influence on Christian theology and Judeo-Islamic philosophies.
Incorrect. The article says his physical science was not replaced systematically until the Enlightenment.

questions.question: What does the article suggest about the relationship between Aristotle's logic and later developments in logic?
options: His logic was the dominant form of Western logic until 19th-century advances in mathematical logic.
His logic was immediately superseded by mathematical logic in the Middle Ages.
His logic was only studied by a few scholars and had little impact.
His logic was considered incomplete by Kant, who improved upon it.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states his conception of logic was the dominant form of Western logic until 19th-century advances in mathematical logic.
Incorrect. The article says his logic remained dominant until the 19th century.
Incorrect. The article says his logic was studied by medieval scholars and influenced logic well into the 19th century.
Incorrect. Kant stated that with Aristotle, logic reached its completion, not that it was incomplete.

questions.question: Why did Aristotle advise Alexander to be 'a leader to the Greeks and a despot to the barbarians'?
options: Because his attitude towards Persia was strongly ethnocentric, viewing Greeks as superior.
Because he wanted Alexander to treat all people equally and justly.
Because he believed that Persians were better suited for democratic rule.
Because he wanted to encourage Alexander to adopt Persian customs and governance.
answer_explanations: Correct. The article says his attitude towards Persia was strongly ethnocentric, and this quote exemplifies that view.
Incorrect. The quote suggests a hierarchical, not equal, treatment.
Incorrect. The quote implies despotic rule for barbarians, not democratic.
Incorrect. The quote suggests a distinction between Greeks and barbarians, not adoption of Persian customs.
